1_parties_and_buyer_credit.value: Seller is Havrebakke Vind ApS; Buyer is Jutland Board & Packaging A/S, which holds no credit rating from a recognised agency. The Buyer's payment obligations are guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S under the Parent Company Guarantee in Annex 4.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.quote: The Buyer's payment obligations under this Agreement are guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S under the Parent Company Guarantee set out in Annex 4.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.note: There is no rating trigger. Section 9.5 is the nearest equivalent: if the Guarantor ceases to hold the entire share capital of the Buyer, or the guarantee ceases to be in force, the Buyer must within 20 Business Days deliver a replacement guarantee acceptable to the Seller or double the Letter of Credit. The document is a draft dated 12 March 2026 and is not binding until signed.

2_facility.value: Onshore wind farm of eight turbine generators with a total installed capacity of 48.0 MW (8 x 6.0 MW). It is at Havrebakke, Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1.
2_facility.quote: The Facility is the Havrebakke Wind Farm, consisting of eight onshore wind turbine generators with a total installed capacity of 48.0 MW located at Havrebakke in Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1, together with the internal cabling, the Havrebakke substation and the ancillary installations described in Annex 1.
2_facility.note: Only one capacity figure (48.0 MW) is given. The document does not label it AC or DC and gives no separate DC figure.

3_supply_period.value: The Supply Period is ten (10) years, starting on the Commercial Operation Date. The Target Commercial Operation Date is 1 October 2027.
3_supply_period.quote: Supply Period: ten (10) years commencing on the Commercial Operation Date.
3_supply_period.clause: Part I, Supply Period; sections 1.1 and 3.3
3_supply_period.note: The start is not a fixed calendar date. The Commercial Operation Date is the date the Seller notifies that the section 3.3 conditions are met: all eight turbines commissioned, grid connected with meters verified, registrations done, and written notice given.

4_cod_and_delay.value: Target Commercial Operation Date is 1 October 2027 and Longstop Date is 31 December 2027. Delay liquidated damages are EUR 9,600 per day, capped at EUR 1,750,000 in aggregate.
4_cod_and_delay.quote: If the Commercial Operation Date has not occurred by the Target Commercial Operation Date of 1 October 2027, the Seller shall pay the Buyer liquidated damages of EUR 9,600 for each day of delay, up to an aggregate cap of EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.clause: Part I, Supply Period; sections 3.4, 3.5 and 3.6; section 1.1
4_cod_and_delay.note: Both dates can be extended day for day for Force Majeure or Buyer breach, up to 180 days in aggregate (3.5). The liquidated damages are the Buyer's sole remedy for delay except termination under 3.6. After the (extended) Longstop Date the Buyer may terminate; no Termination Amount is payable, and accrued liquidated damages are still owed.

5_price_and_indexation.value: The Contract Price is EUR 58.00 per MWh, exclusive of VAT, applicable to each MWh of Metered Output from the Commercial Operation Date. There is no indexation: the price is fixed for the Supply Period.
5_price_and_indexation.quote: Contract Price: EUR 58.00 per MWh, exclusive of value added tax, applicable to each MWh of Metered Output from the Commercial Operation Date.
5_price_and_indexation.clause: Annex 2 (Election Sheet); referenced in Part I, Price and section 7.1
5_price_and_indexation.note: The price is stated only in Annex 2, not in the body; Annex 2 prevails. Annex 2 says: 'Indexation: none. The Contract Price is fixed for the Supply Period and shall not be indexed.' Because there is no indexation, there is no start date or share. Section 11.2 lets the Parties negotiate a price adjustment after a Change in Law, which sits uneasily with Part I saying price adjustment is governed exclusively by Annex 2.

6_volume_and_performance.value: Pay-as-produced: the Buyer takes 100% of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production is 158,000 MWh (P50) and Minimum Annual Production is 118,500 MWh (75% of P50). If output falls below the minimum, the Seller pays a shortfall payment capped at EUR 500,000 per Contract Year.
6_volume_and_performance.quote: If in any Contract Year the Metered Output is less than the Minimum Annual Production, the Seller shall pay the Buyer a shortfall payment equal to the shortfall in MWh multiplied by the amount, if positive, by which the average day-ahead price for bidding zone DK1 for that Contract Year exceeds the Contract Price, capped at EUR 500,000 per Contract Year.
6_volume_and_performance.clause: Part I, Contract Quantity and Volume Structure; sections 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, 4.6; Annex 1; Annex 2
6_volume_and_performance.note: The guarantee is an annual minimum production, not an availability guarantee. The shortfall payment is zero when the DK1 day-ahead average is at or below the Contract Price. The minimum is pro-rated in the first and last Contract Year and reduced for Force Majeure, TSO-instructed reductions and Buyer breach (4.5, 4.6).

7_product_and_certificates.value: The Buyer buys electricity at the Delivery Point plus all Guarantees of Origin issued for the Metered Output. The Guarantees of Origin are transferred at no additional cost, and no capacity product, ancillary service or other attribute is sold.
7_product_and_certificates.quote: Product: electricity generated by the Facility and delivered at the Delivery Point, together with all Guarantees of Origin issued in respect of the Metered Output.
7_product_and_certificates.clause: Part I, Product and Certificates; section 8
7_product_and_certificates.note: Guarantees of Origin go to the Buyer's registry account within 15 Business Days after issue (8.1), with no separate price. The Seller need not procure replacement Guarantees of Origin for a production shortfall (8.2). Certificates under any replacement scheme are also transferred at no cost (8.3).

8_curtailment.value: The only curtailment the document addresses is output reduction instructed by the Transmission System Operator. The Buyer pays nothing for it, any compensation from the Transmission System Operator belongs to the Seller, and such reductions lower the Minimum Annual Production for the shortfall test.
8_curtailment.quote: Reductions of output instructed by the transmission system operator shall not give rise to any payment by the Buyer.
8_curtailment.note: The document gives the Buyer no right to curtail, sets no cap in hours or MWh, and does not pay curtailed energy as deemed delivered. The deemed quantity in 5.5 is used only to adjust the minimum production. Negative prices are not mentioned anywhere, and the Buyer must take 100% of Metered Output (4.1). Searched the full text for curtailment, deemed quantity, negative prices and output reductions.

9_delivery_point_and_balancing.value: Settlement is physical, with title and risk passing to the Buyer at the Delivery Point, the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation. The Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears all imbalance costs from the Commercial Operation Date.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.quote: The Buyer shall appoint the balance responsible party for the Facility and shall bear all imbalance costs from the Commercial Operation Date.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.clause: Part I, Settlement and Delivery Point and Balancing; sections 4.2 and 5.2; Annex 2
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.note: There is no financial reference price because settlement is physical. The Seller provides day-ahead and intraday production forecasts to the balance responsible party, without warranty (5.1).

10_credit_support.value: Seller gives a EUR 2,000,000 bank guarantee within 10 Business Days after Financial Close, valid until 12 months after the Commercial Operation Date. Buyer gives the Parent Company Guarantee plus a letter of credit equal to six months of expected payments, delivered at least 30 days before expected commercial operation and kept in force until 60 days after the Supply Period ends.
10_credit_support.quote: The Seller shall deliver a bank guarantee in the amount of EUR 2,000,000 within ten (10) Business Days after Financial Close, to remain in force until twelve (12) months after the Commercial Operation Date.
10_credit_support.clause: Part I, Credit Support; section 9 (9.1 to 9.5); Annex 3; Annex 4
10_credit_support.note: The Buyer's letter of credit is six twelfths of Expected Annual Production times the Contract Price, recalculated each 1 January. By my calculation that is about EUR 4.58 million at EUR 58.00/MWh; the document states no figure. Both banks must be rated at least A-. The Parent Company Guarantee stays in force until all amounts are paid in full (Annex 4, clause 6).

11_default_and_termination.value: Events of Default include non-payment (10 Business Days after notice), failure to deliver or replace credit support, insolvency, uncured material breach (30 days) and unauthorised assignment, plus Seller failure to reach commercial operation by the Longstop Date and Buyer Guarantor insolvency or guarantee failure. The Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remaining Supply Period, discounted at the Danish central bank reference rate plus 2 points, determined by the Non-Defaulting Party.
11_default_and_termination.quote: The Termination Amount shall be the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price for the Expected Annual Production over the remainder of the Supply Period, discounted at the reference rate of the Danish central bank plus two (2) percentage points, and determined by the Non-Defaulting Party as at the early termination date, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.
11_default_and_termination.clause: Sections 12.1, 13.2 to 13.6; Reference Forward Price in section 1.1; production profile factor in Annex 2
11_default_and_termination.note: The calculation is fully specified in the attached document: Reference Forward Price is defined in 1.1 and the 0.88 profile factor is in Annex 2. The amount is payable only if it is a loss for the Non-Defaulting Party; if it is a gain, nothing is payable by either Party (13.4). It is the exclusive remedy for loss of bargain (13.5). Terminations under 2.3, 3.6, 10.4 or 11.3 carry no Termination Amount (13.6).

12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.value: If a Change in Law raises a Party's cost by more than EUR 250,000 in any Contract Year, the Parties must negotiate in good faith an adjustment, which may include the Contract Price. If none is agreed within 90 days, the affected Party may terminate on 60 days' notice with no Termination Amount. Force Majeure lasting more than 180 consecutive days lets either Party terminate on 30 days' notice, also with no Termination Amount.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.quote: If a Change in Law increases the cost to a Party of performing this Agreement by more than EUR 250,000 in any Contract Year, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an adjustment to restore the economic balance of this Agreement, which may include an adjustment to the Contract Price.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.note: The cost allocation sits partly under Taxes, Levies and Regulatory Costs: the Seller bears taxes and charges on generation and injection, the Buyer those on offtake, transport, consumption or resale (17.2). New taxes are allocated the same way and are subject to section 11 above the threshold (17.3). The document does not say expressly who bears a change-in-law cost below the EUR 250,000 threshold beyond that split. Corporate income tax of general application is excluded from Change in Law. The price-adjustment possibility in 11.2 conflicts with the Annex 2 statement that the price is fixed.
